content:
alex: quick follow-up from the RFC — we talked about soft-eviction and leasing, but one thing that didn't get a lot of airtime: deterministic replay for incident debugging. we should be able to reconstruct exact batch composition for a given window. :thinking:

maria: +1. reproducing a tail latency spike locally would save hours. curious how far we want to bake determinism into the runtime vs keep it as an optional debug mode.

sam: idea: attach lightweight boundary markers to every enqueue that include a small per-request seed and a source tag. then batches can carry the marker vector so we can replay the same grouping. something like:

```json
{"marker_v1": {"seed": "0x9af", "enqueue_idx": 12345, "src": "api-v2"}}
```

katie: that could work, but markers increase token metadata. need to measure perf impact. also how do we handle preemption/requeue? markers must survive soft-eviction and re-enqueue.

alex: good point. proposal: markers are only present while tracing is enabled (sampling). default runtime doesn't attach them. when sampling is on we also flag requests as "replayable" so KV-cache pointers are recorded in the replay trace.

jordan: ok but we must be careful: replay should not change semantics. if replay pulls from cache differently it will diverge. we need to include cache-hit-ids in the trace so replay knows whether a KV hit occurred at enqueue time.

maria: so trace record = batch markers + per-request cache-hints + scheduling decisions (was preempted, evicted, coalesced window id). with that we can deterministically re-run the scheduler emulator and step through the exact batching decisions.

sam: here's a minimal on-disk trace layout suggestion (proto-ish):

```yaml
trace_v1:
  window_id: 2026-03-21T12:34:00Z
  seed: 0x9af
  requests:
    - req_id: r-12
      enqueue_idx: 12345
      kvcache_id: kvc-332 (or null)
      preempted: false
    - req_id: r-13
      enqueue_idx: 12346
      kvcache_id: null
      preempted: true
  batches:
    - batch_id: b-1
      members: [r-12, r-13]
      kernels_used: [gemm-v2]
```

katie: tests must cover: 1) identical grouping under same seed, 2) identical ordering when preemption happened, 3) kvcache hit/miss parity. also ensure sampling overhead <1% p50 in a stress run.

alex: ops question: where do we store traces? we could push to long-term object storage for sampled windows only, and expose a console flow that rehydrates into a local scheduler emulator. privacy: traces must redact prompt text. only structural metadata + cache ids.

jordan: add note — for customers on Dedicated/Private, traces should respect isolation: either stored in customer-owned bucket or never leave their VPC.

maria: another practical thing: if a batch contains requests from multiple model variants (fallback flow), replay needs to account for model substitution decisions. include model_variant tag per request.

sam: we should also emit a short deterministic id for each batch that is a function of (window_seed, sorted enqueue_idx list). that can be used as a compact key for comparing traces across environments. e.g. `batch_fingerprint = sha1(seed || join(enqueue_idx))`.

katie: ops/infra: this does create a new telemetry surface. we need sampling config (rate, tag filters, store destination), retention policy, and a small schema versioning plan so we can evolve markers without breaking old traces.

alex: ok next: how does this change admission interface? we could add an optional `trace_marker` field on enqueue RPC: `enqueue(payload, trace_marker=null)`. runtime defaults to null. if set, admission must propagate marker across preemption and into the eventual batch object.

jordan: micro detail: if a request is split (microbatching into two GPU slices), we should either duplicate marker with part index or attach a `part_count`/`part_idx` tuple. prefer keeping single logical request id and a parts array in the trace to avoid ambiguity.

maria: UX for devs: Console -> select window -> click "Replay" -> emulator runs with same seed and outputs batch boundaries and simulated per-request latencies. super helpful for investigating queuing races.

sam: implementation plan:
- add marker plumbing to enqueue/dequeue paths (opt-in)
- small on-path cost test: run 1% sampled with markers in staging, compare p50/p99
- storage pipeline to archive traces to s3 (or customer bucket) with redaction step
- emulator binary in devex repo that can ingest trace and replay scheduler decisions

alex: security note: redaction must remove prompt text and any PII. only include hashed IDs for cache keys. infra-bot: run redaction-check on sample traces? :eyes:

infra-bot: redaction-check queued for sample trace batch-2026-03-21T12:34 (job id 8812). will post results.

katie: final design question for reviewers: do we make replay deterministic only for trace mode, or try to align default runtime to be deterministic (at cost of some runtime complexity)? I'm leaning trace-only for now.

maria: agree. keep production fast/loose, but provide a deterministic trace mode for ops/debug. we can revisit if customers demand hard determinism.

alex: cool. i'll write up a short RFC follow-up with the enqueue API change, trace schema, and a small benchmark plan. will ping reviewers. thanks all. :shipit:
